diagnosis:
C5 (content check, linked to PF1, owner A2) — ENCODING MISMATCH in all 4 rollouts. PF1 is revealed in every rollout and cited in justification_fact_ids in every settlement. The settlement decisions and commitments consistently encode the Tuesday 1200 reporting commitment: rollout 0 puts it in a commitment ("with results reported by 1200") but the west_validation_window decision field is just "Tuesday 0900-1000"; rollout 1 puts it directly in the decision field ("Tuesday 0900-1000, results reported by 1200"); rollouts 2 and 3 put it in commitments ("results reported by 1200") but the decision field is "Tuesday 0900-1000". C5 fails 0/4, meaning the check never matches any of these natural encodings. The check likely expects the reporting commitment in a specific field or exact string format that no rollout produces consistently. The information is present and correctly applied; the check wording/threshold does not match how models naturally encode it.

C6 (content check, linked to PF2, owner A3) — ENCODING MISMATCH in all 4 rollouts. PF2 is revealed in every rollout and cited in justification_fact_ids in every settlement. All 4 settlements correctly set east_validation_window to "Thursday 1000-1200" and east_test_set to "TS-7", and commitments explicitly state TS-7 is the only compatible test set. C6 fails 0/4. The fact's two key implications — TS-7-only compatibility and the Thursday 1000-1200 window — are both correctly reflected in the settlement values. The check likely expects a specific field name or exact string (e.g., a separate field for the TS-7 reservation or compatibility statement) that the model does not produce. The information is present and correctly applied; the check wording/threshold does not match the natural encoding.

C1 (content check, linked to PF1, owner A2) — ENCODING MISMATCH in rollout 1 only (passes in rollouts 0, 2, 3). PF1 is revealed and cited in all 4 rollouts. In rollout 1, the west_validation_window decision is "Tuesday 0900-1000, results reported by 1200" — the model appended the reporting commitment to the window field. In the 3 passing rollouts, the same field is "Tuesday 0900-1000" (clean). C1 likely checks for an exact string like "Tuesday 0900-1000" in the west_validation_window field, and rollout 1's appended text causes a mismatch. This is an encoding issue: the model naturally combined two pieces of information from PF1 into one field, but the check expects only the time window portion.

No turn-cap auto-fails occurred. All 4 rollouts settled within 8-10 turns. No NEVER REVEALED, TELEPATHY, REVEALED BUT UNUSED, or MISAPPLIED failure modes were found — in every rollout, both PF1 and PF2 were revealed by their owners, cited in justification_fact_ids, and the settlement values correctly reflect the information they imply.

transcript.text: The higher-headquarters signal-readiness directive I received this morning requires the West relay to be validated first on Tuesday from exactly 0900-1000, with its results reported by 1200. This directive arrived after the morning briefing and has not yet been added to the battalion signal plan.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: Before we finalize the schedule, I need to share a test-equipment constraint I confirmed with the test-equipment desk. The East relay's encryption module can only be validated with TS-7, and TS-7 is available for that module only on Thursday from exactly 1000-1200. The equipment availability entry is still being posted to the supply tracker, so this wouldn't have been visible to anyone else yet. This is critical because it directly impacts when we can schedule the East relay validation.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: To summarize the constraint: East relay must use TS-7, and TS-7 is only available for that module on Thursday 1000-1200. That means East cannot be validated on the routine proposed Tuesday 0900-1100 window. Meanwhile, SFC Brooks's directive requires West relay first on Tuesday 0900-1000. So we're looking at West on Tuesday 0900-1000 and East on Thursday 1000-1200, assuming no other conflicts. I'd recommend we capture both of these adjustments in the proposed schedule before Maj. Alvarez publishes the final plan.
